Draft a complete reply for the following Gmail conversation in plain text only. User mailbox: surojitdutta1812@gmail.com
The sender: Magicbricks <feed.alrt@magicbricks.com>
The sender sent the following email/thread to the user mailbox. Draft a reply FROM the user mailbox TO the sender. Do not adopt the sender's role, organization, duties, apologies, or responsibilities. Use User_reply_intent to express the mailbox owner's position, complaint, preference, question, or response. If User_reply_intent criticizes the sender's service, write the reply as criticism from the user to the sender, not as an apology from the sender/provider side. Use only the thread messages below to understand the conversation history. The thread messages are chronological; the newest thread message is the current/latest email. Mentally convert them into: Current message with sender/content, then Previous messages as numbered datetime | sender | action lines. Greet first if appropriate with hi/hello/dear, then respond to the latest message. Close naturally with regards, best wishes, or another suitable closing when appropriate. Do not add facts that are not present in the message, thread, summary, or user intent. Use Summary_JSON as helpful context only, but prefer the actual message/thread if they differ. Write a useful reply body, but keep it bounded by the user's intent and known facts. Acknowledge every question, request, date, requirement, constraint, or next step that needs a response, but do not answer unavailable details or create a solution that the user did not authorize. Follow User_reply_intent closely; if the intent is empty, draft a neutral helpful reply that fits the latest/current message and covers the relevant details. Treat User_reply_intent as the strongest signal for what the user is willing to say. Do not introduce new assurances that are not explicitly present in User_reply_intent or the thread, including promises of action, compensation, timelines, confirmations, communication channels, responsibility or blame, and conditional outcomes. If User_reply_intent is brief, keep the reply brief and only express the stated intent. When the sender asks for a result that the user has not authorized, acknowledge the request but do not grant, deny, schedule, promise, or conditionally commit to that result. If User_reply_intent says the user is checking, reviewing, investigating, confirming, or looking into something, only say that the matter is being checked/reviewed/investigated/confirmed and that the sender will be updated when confirmed information is available. Do not add speculative causes, internal records, team actions, policy conditions, dates, follow-up windows, refund conditions, delivery estimates, or outcomes. Respond to the latest sender and latest ask, while respecting dates, cancellations, scheduling context, and earlier thread details. Do not invent availability, promises, attachments, payments, project details, logistics explanations, investigation findings, operational outcomes, or facts. If information is missing, ask a clear clarification instead of making it up. Return only the reply body. Do not return JSON, labels, reasoning, markdown, or tool calls.
